**Gain** and **volume** both make a channel louder, so they are easy to confuse. On the X32 they are at
opposite ends of the strip, and for a good reason.

- **Gain** (top of the strip, in Config/Preamp) sets how much the *microphone* signal is amplified *before*
  anything else happens. It decides the level going into the gate, the EQ, the compressor and the
  converter. Set it once, at the sound check.
- **The fader** (bottom of the strip) sets how loud that channel is *in the mix*. You ride it during the show.

## Why gain comes first

The X32's preamps have a 72 dB gain range and clip at +23 dBu. Past that, the converter writes the biggest
number it can and cuts the top off the wave. That is **clipping**, and nothing later in the strip can undo it,
the fader included: a clipped signal turned down is just a quieter clipped signal.

Too little gain is a problem too. The fader only goes to **+10 dB**. If the gain is far too low you run out
of fader, and the gate and compressor, whose thresholds are set in dB, never see the level they expect.

<div class="sk-care">Rule of thumb: set the gain so the <b>loudest</b> part of the song peaks around
<b>−12 to −6</b> on the channel meter, never in the red. Then bring the fader up to around 0 dB. If the fader
ends up near the top or the bottom to get a good balance, go back and fix the gain.</div>

## Try it: the quiet talker

A speaker at a podium, quietly, a little far from the mic. The Gain starts much too low.

<div class="lk" data-w="strip" data-source="speech" data-show="pre fader" data-goal="gain" data-set="gain=22,fdb=10"
  data-tries="Too low, fader at +10:gain=22,fdb=10;Way too hot, fader down:gain=72,fdb=-20;Too hot:gain=66,fdb=0;Right:gain=52,fdb=0"></div>

1. Press ▶. The fader is already at **+10**, the top, and it's still quiet; the meter barely moves.
2. Pull the fader back to 0 dB and raise the **Gain** until the peaks sit between −12 and −6. Press **Check my
   channel**.
3. Try **Way too hot, fader down**: the output meter looks safe, but the **CLIP** light has latched and it
   sounds broken. Turning down the fader didn't help.

Notice the hiss: with the gain very high (around +60), the preamp's own noise comes up with it.

## Gain moves everything after it

Change the gain *after* setting a gate or a compressor and they stop working properly, because their
thresholds stay where they were while the signal moves. On this kick drum the gate is set well.

<div class="lk" data-w="strip" data-source="kick" data-show="pre gate fader" data-goal="gate"
  data-set="gate=1,gthr=-32,gatt=0.5,ghold=20,grel=120"
  data-tries="Gate set well:gain=24;Then gain −10:gain=14;Then gain +10:gain=34"></div>

With the gain 10 dB lower, quieter kicks fall below the threshold and get lost; 10 dB higher and the snare
bleed starts opening the gate. That is why the order is always: **gain first**, then everything else.

## On the X32

- The **gain** knob is at the top left of the channel strip. Its LED collar shows the setting; the screen
  (View) shows the number.
- The **meter** next to it, and the meter on the fader strip, are the input level. The screen meter goes up to
  **clip**.
- Mute a channel before switching **48 V** on or off (the manual's advice), and don't touch the gain right after:
  it can pop.
- Gain on the X32 is for the local inputs and stage boxes. If a channel comes from USB or a card, its trim is
  digital (±18 dB).
